preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 1500 and 1 <= m <= 1500 for n, m in [(int(stdin.split()[0]), int(stdin.split()[1]))])
preconditions.description: Input dimensions n and m are within bounds 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 1500.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_ij <= n for i in range(n) for j in range(m) for a_ij in [int(stdin.split()[i*m + j])])
preconditions.description: All elements in table A are integers between 1 and n (inclusive).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= b_ij <= n for i in range(n) for j in range(m) for b_ij in [int(stdin.split()[n*m + i*m + j])])
preconditions.description: All elements in table B are integers between 1 and n (inclusive).
Input is well-formed with exactly n*m elements for A, n*m elements for B, and two integers for n and m.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (all(1 <= int(c) <= m for c in stdout.split()[1:]) and len(stdout.split()) - 1 <= 5001)
postconditions.description: If no solution exists, output is '-1'. Otherwise, output is a valid sequence of column indices (1 ≤ c_i ≤ m) with length k ≤ 5000.

postconditions.expression: all(all(b_ij == a_ij for i, j in zip(range(n), range(m))) for a_ij, b_ij in zip(parse_table_A(stdin), parse_table_B(stdin))) if stdout.strip() == '-1' else False
postconditions.description: If output is '-1', it means no sequence of column sortings can transform A into B.

postconditions.expression: all(all(b_ij == a_ij for i, j in zip(range(n), range(m))) for a_ij, b_ij in zip(apply_sort_sequence(parse_table_A(stdin), [int(c) for c in stdout.split()[1:]]), parse_table_B(stdin))) if stdout.strip() != '-1' else False
postconditions.description: If output is a sequence of columns, applying those sortings to A must yield B.
